goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:78 — A granted all-clients view permission short-circuits evaluation of an explicit deny for an individual client, exposing clients that administrators intended to exclude.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at ClientPermissionsV2.java:78, the canView(ClientModel client) method returns true if canView() returns true (line 78-79). The canView() method at line 84 returns true if canViewClientDefault() OR hasPermission(VIEW) for all clients. This means if a user has VIEW permission on all-clients resource type, canView(client) will return true immediately without checking if there's a specific deny permission for that individual client. The hasPermission(client, VIEW) check on line 82 that would evaluate individual client permissions is never reached when the all-clients permission grants access. This is a real authorization bypass bug where explicit deny permissions on individual clients are ignored when an all-clients view permission exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:70 — Existing realms with initialized admin permissions never receive the new Clients resource or scopes because init returns immediately for an existing permission client, preventing client permission creation after upgrade.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that existing realms won't receive the new Clients resource because 'init returns immediately for an existing permission client'. However, the diff does not show any 'init' method or initialization logic. The diff shows AdminPermissionsSchema being updated to include CLIENTS in the schema Map, and the getOrCreateResource method which handles resource creation on-demand. The finding references behavior ('init returns immediately') that is not visible in this diff. The schema changes shown would apply to the static SCHEMA instance used throughout the codebase.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:73 — Existing FGAP V2 realms never receive the new Clients resource or scopes because init returns when the permissions client exists, so client permission creation fails after upgrading.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims there's an issue with 'init' returning early when the permissions client exists, preventing new Clients resource/scopes from being added during upgrades. However, examining the diff, there is no 'init' method shown or modified. The diff shows changes to AdminPermissionsSchema.java adding CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE and related constants, but there's no evidence of an initialization flow that would skip adding new resources to existing realms. The finding references behavior (init returning early) that is not visible in the provided diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:78 — An all-clients view grant makes canView(client) return before evaluating a client-specific denial, exposing clients that resource-specific permissions exclude.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at ClientPermissionsV2.canView(ClientModel client) at line 78-83: it first checks canView() which includes hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW) for all-clients. If this returns true, the method returns true immediately without checking for any client-specific denial permissions. This is different from the pattern in canManage(client) which only checks the all-clients permission via hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE) which does evaluate resource-specific permissions. The test code in UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest shows the expected pattern where negative/denial permissions on specific resources should override positive all-resource permissions (see testViewUserPermissionDenyByDefault). The canView(client) implementation shortcuts this by returning early on all-clients VIEW permission.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:78 — Calling canView() before evaluating the client grants callers with an all-clients view permission access even when a client-specific policy denies it, bypassing that client's access restriction.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at ClientPermissionsV2.canView(ClientModel client) at line 78, it first calls canView() (the no-argument version) which checks for all-clients VIEW permission. If that returns true, it immediately returns true without checking client-specific permissions. This means if a user has all-clients VIEW permission but there's a NEGATIVE policy denying access to a specific client, the denial would be bypassed because canView() returns true before hasPermission(client, VIEW) is evaluated. This is inconsistent with how canManage(ClientModel) works at line 68, which only checks the all-clients permission via hasOneAdminRole, not via hasPermission. The pattern in UserPermissionsV2 shows that client-specific negative policies should be able to override all-resource permissions, but this implementation short-circuits that check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:78 — An all-clients VIEW grant bypasses client-specific denying permissions because canView() returns before evaluating the target, an authorization regression left uncovered by the new view tests.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the canView(ClientModel client) method in ClientPermissionsV2.java lines 77-83, it checks canView() OR canConfigure(client) first, and if either is true, returns true. Then it checks hasPermission(client, VIEW). The finding claims this is a bug because 'all-clients VIEW grant bypasses client-specific denying permissions'. However, this is the intended design pattern - the method is checking if the user has ANY permission to view (either global view, configure on specific client, or specific view permission). The hasPermission method with a specific client (line 83) handles client-specific permissions. There's no evidence in the diff that client-specific denying permissions should override global grants - this would be a design decision, not a bug. The test testViewAllClients() in PermissionClientTest.java tests the VIEW permission and doesn't indicate any expectation of client-specific denial overriding global grants.
